title: Normalized derived scalar-data models
statement: Fix a category C with object universe c and morphism universe v, a Grothendieck topology J and an EssentiallySmall.{max c v r} instance. Let B and F be towers of commutative ring sheaves in universe max c v r, with transitions tau and sigma, and let alpha_n : B_(n) to F_(n) satisfy alpha_(n+1) followed by sigma_n equals tau_n followed by alpha_n. For the ordinary system models, there exists normalized derived change-of-rings data for the system map and for every level map alpha_n, including the ordinary and derived adjunctions and their representative normalization equations.

proof.text: Apply the existing normalized arbitrary sheaf-ring scalar model theorem to a ring map on any essentially small site. Retain its cochain derived model, ordinary adjunction and derived adjunction. Its ordinary unit is systemModelTmul with scalar 1. Cancel the two inverse object-identification maps and use one_smul to obtain exactly extensionUnit in ScalarData.unit_section.

Postcompose the existing normalized cochain transpose equation by the hom component of mapDerivedCategoryFactors. Its inverse followed by its hom cancels, giving ScalarData.transpose_model. The theorem provides this equation for all complexes, hence in particular for the K-flat complexes required here.

The vertical sequence site is essentially small by sequenceSmall. Apply the preceding conversion on that site to the compatible system ring map, and on J to each level map alpha_n, and combine the two conclusions.

proof_origin.place: Construction 4.1 and Lemma 4.10; reuse of the normalized generic model lem-pur-system-scalar-model, with the same conversion already proved privately in SemilinearSystemsExistence.

theorem semilinearScalarData
    (F : ℕ → Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r})
    (σ : ∀ n : ℕ, F (n + 1) ⟶ F n) (α : ∀ n : ℕ, B n ⟶ F n)
    (hα : ∀ n : ℕ, α (n + 1) ≫ σ n = τ n ≫ α n) :
    Nonempty (ScalarData.{c, v, max c v r}
      (systemMap.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ F σ α hα)) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty (ScalarData.{c, v, max c v r} (α n))
